scope: 500 native128 NPC skin masters and100 native128 outfit masters, plus600 Java64 derivatives
review_method: Inspected assembled front/back catalogue contact sheets, then re-inspected the updated character overview and first fashion sheet after lower-garment drape changes. These are orthographic UV assemblies, not in-game screenshots.
findings: Occupation-specific police caps, badges, radios, healthcare stethoscopes, rescue reflective bands, food aprons/caps, courier shoulder straps, lanyards and media equipment are readable in the previews.
Boss and five supplied initial prisoner appearances are distinct; original identity and custody flags remain unchanged.

Traditional garments continue onto the leg UVs, with separate draped hems, borders and pleats; formal tailoring, sports sleeves/shorts and utility equipment are represented within the existing classic player silhouette.
Native128 strand clusters, eye corners, garment seams and stitch details are actual source pixels rather than a simple enlarged64 image.
Final six-face UV review corrected cropped cap undersides: the head-overlay bottom face remains transparent, so cap fabric does not appear below the chin.

The64 export initially discarded single-pixel seams with point sampling and produced duplicate outfit derivatives. UV-aligned2x2 area reduction with binary alpha fixed this; all100 outfit derivatives and500 NPC derivatives now have distinct pixel hashes.

reproducibility_check.command_summary: Regenerated every master in memory with the committed generator, compared all pixel bytes to saved masters, then reproduced and compared all64 compatibility derivatives.

limitations: Visual uniqueness means distinct visible character artwork, not600 separate character meshes.
Outfit overlay application, signed NPC texture hosting, custody outfit switching and actual Java/Bedrock rendering are not implemented or verified by this art batch.
The original records contain legacy world anchors; this generation does not validate or authorize those locations.
